text: For #622: every workload container Invariant starts with docker run or create gets a CPU quota, 4 CPUs by default, so one sandbox or model check can't take a whole machine's cores while a person works on it, as a factory sandbox took about 10 of 18 on 2026-11-05. One host setting, INVARIANT_CONTAINER_CPUS, changes the default: unset or empty means 4, finite decimal counts of at least 0.01 are accepted, and anything else fails with a named error before a container or its image is started, while cleanup still works. Explicit limits win, so the Python application executor keeps its 1 CPU, 512 MiB and 128 processes, and memory, process, isolation, cleanup and deadline rules are unchanged. The quota is per container, not a host-wide budget, and Docker-managed image builds are outside it. Both agent backends pass the setting to their MCP servers, so the watcher, dashboard, CLI and their check processes agree, and changing it means restarting them. The sandbox's two timeout fixtures moved from a one-second phase to fifteen seconds inside a ninety-second run, shown with a three-second slow-start stand-in, because a one-second phase failed under the quota.
